      What a Sunday morning looks like

      Most first-time guests come to the 9:00 service. Here is the morning from start to finish, so nothing catches you off guard.

      1. 9:00 am · Sanctuary

        Divine Service

        Our worship centers on God's gifts in His Word and Sacraments. Jesus meets us with forgiveness, life and salvation, and we respond with prayer, praise and thanksgiving. Expect hymns led by our 1966 pipe organ, Scripture, a sermon and the Lord's Supper, in about an hour.

      2. 10:15 am · Fellowship Hall

        Coffee hour

        Stay for coffee and conversation. This is the easiest time to meet Pastor Ben and the congregation.

      3. 10:30 am · Cafeteria

        Education hour

        Adults study the Bible together while children 4 and up go to Sonshine Club.

      Read what we believe, then let Pastor Ben talk it through with you over coffee. Email him at pastorben@bethlehemlcms.com or call the church office to set up a time.

      What we believe

      Saved by grace, through faith, in Christ alone

      As a congregation of the Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod, we confess the faith taught in Holy Scripture and summarized in the Lutheran Confessions. Here is the heart of those teachings.

      1. Scripture

        2 Timothy 3:15–16

        The Bible is God's inspired Word, written by holy men and without error.

      2. The Triune God

        Matthew 3:16–17

        There is one true God: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, three distinct Persons in one divine being.

      3. God the Father

        Genesis 1:1

        The Father Almighty created heaven and earth and all creatures, and He loves us as His children.

      4. Jesus Christ

        John 1:1–2

        Jesus is true God, begotten of the Father from eternity, and true man, born of the Virgin Mary. He is our Savior and Lord.

      5. The Holy Spirit

        Titus 3:4–8

        The Spirit creates faith through the Gospel and Baptism, and keeps us in faith through the Lord's Supper and God's Word.

      6. Sin

        Romans 8:1–4

        Every person is born sinful and separated from God, and we sin in thought, word and deed.

      7. Salvation in Christ

        John 3:16

        Christ fulfilled the Law in our place, died for our sins and rose again. Salvation comes only through Him, never through our own works.

      8. Faith

        Ephesians 2:8–9

        Salvation is God's free gift, received by faith. Each person is called to confess Jesus as Savior.

      9. Law and Gospel

        Romans 3:23–24

        The Law shows how God wants us to live and where we fall short. The Gospel proclaims our salvation in Jesus Christ.

      10. Forgiveness and mission

        Matthew 28:18–20

        God daily and richly forgives our sins by grace, for Christ's sake. The church's mission is to bring this Gospel to all people.

      Food Bank · Serving since the 1980s

      Groceries for our neighbors, three mornings a week

      Our food bank began during the early-1980s recession, when factory closings hit southeast Fort Wayne hard. Today it is a partner of Associated Churches and Community Harvest, and our volunteers stock produce, frozen meat, bread, eggs, dairy and pantry staples.

      Mission, vision & values

      A catalyst for Gospel transformation in southeast Fort Wayne

      Our vision is a neighborhood where all people experience Christ's love, grow in faith, and restore hope together. Our mission has three parts.

      Proclaiming Christ

      We center everything on Jesus, grounding ourselves in biblical truth and the historic Christian faith. Knowing people encounter the gospel in unique ways, we proclaim Christ clearly and live out His love, mercy, and justice with faithfulness to Scripture and sensitivity to our neighbors. Our worship, teaching, and community life bear witness to His grace in word and deed.

      Nurturing Faith

      We nurture faith as a shared journey where people of all backgrounds and generations encounter God's transforming grace. Through relationships shaped by mutual honor and discipleship across all ages, we pass on faith, learn from one another, and grow together as God's family. We celebrate the richness of His kingdom, where the gospel restores dignity, unites us across every divide, and calls us into a new identity in Christ.

      Restoring Hope

      We are called to be Christ's presence in our neighborhood, particularly southeast Fort Wayne, recognizing the dignity and strength already present in our community. Believing that God's light shines in all circumstances, we engage in partnerships that foster mutual transformation and lasting flourishing.

      Our values

      • We are Christ-CenteredJesus is at the heart of everything we do. His grace shapes our worship, relationships, and mission.
      • We Stand on God's WordWe are rooted in the historic Christian faith, committed to the authority of Scripture as God's infallible Word that guides our beliefs, decisions, and practices in an ever-changing world.
      • We Embody the GospelWe proclaim and live out the gospel, demonstrating Christ's love, mercy, and justice so that all may know His grace, restoration, and belonging.
      • We Celebrate God's Diverse KingdomWe rejoice that the gospel unites all people in Christ. We seek to reflect this diversity in our life together and actively pursue unity and reconciliation in our community.
      • We Nurture Faith Across All AgesThe church is a family where faith is passed from one generation to the next. We value deep relationships across all ages, nurturing discipleship in both young and old.
      • We Have Hope for Our NeighborhoodTrusting that Christ is already at work in southeast Fort Wayne, we walk alongside and work with our neighbors, partnering for mutual flourishing and lasting hope.
      • We Accomplish More Together Than AloneWe recognize that the work of the kingdom is bigger than us. With humility and joy, we collaborate with others who share our heart for gospel-centered community engagement.
      • We are Generous with God's GiftsWe faithfully steward the gifts God has entrusted to us, our time, resources, and building, so that they may be used for His kingdom and the flourishing of others.

      Our history

      A hundred years on the south side

      Bethlehem began as a branch school for families of Zion and Concordia who lived on the southeast side. Forty-six men signed our constitution in 1926, and we turn 100 this year.

      1. 1926

        Congregation organized; joins the Missouri Synod the next spring.

      2. 1930

        Church-and-school building dedicated on Anthony Boulevard.

      3. 1940

        Today's church building dedicated on August 4.

      4. 1958

        693 students make ours the largest LCMS elementary school.

      5. 1965

        Three new bells installed and dedicated.

      6. 1966

        Our pipe organ is dedicated on March 27.

      7. 1980

        Food bank founded with Associated Churches.

      8. 2009

        Our school joins Zion and Unity to form Lutheran South Unity School.

      We are generous with God's gifts

      We steward our time, our resources and our building so they can be used for His kingdom and the flourishing of others.

      Fellowship

      Women of Bethlehem

      Women of Bethlehem (WOB) brings the women of our congregation together for service and study, and builds Christian friendship along the way. Every woman of Bethlehem is also a member of the Lutheran Women in Mission (LWML).

      "This service that you perform is not only supplying the needs of the Lord's people but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanks to God." 2 Corinthians 9:12

      Worship

      Choir & handbells

      Our choir and handbell choir lead the congregation in song and help us praise God in worship, alongside our 1966 pipe organ.

      Interested in singing or ringing? Call the church office at (260) 744-3228 to find out when rehearsals meet.

      Care

      Stephen Ministry

      Stephen Ministry is one-to-one Christian care for people going through a hard time. A Stephen Minister is a caring Christian friend who listens and offers emotional and spiritual support.

      • Each Stephen Minister completes 50 hours of training in confidential, Christ-centered care.
      • They care for one person at a time, meeting about an hour each week.
      • Men are matched with men, and women with women.
      • Stephen Ministers meet with their leaders twice a month for supervision and continuing education.

      To ask about receiving care, or to become a Stephen Minister, call the church office at (260) 744-3228.

      Missions

      Sharing the Gospel beyond Anthony Boulevard

      Liberia · Since 2004

      Liberian Children's Mission

      Joe Boway was born in Liberia and came to the U.S. in 1990 because of the civil war. While studying at Taylor University, he did his student teaching at Bethlehem. In 2004 New Life Lutheran Church in Fort Wayne commissioned him as a missionary to Liberia, and Bethlehem held a fundraising drive to help him start Christian schools for children who had lost years of education to the war.

      14 schoolsmore than 5,000 students
      $25pays for one child's schooling for a year

      More than three in four new students come from families outside the church. Joe travels to Liberia regularly to train staff and assess needs, and Bethlehem has helped fill Orphan Grain Train shipping containers with computers, furniture, supplies and books.

      To receive Joe's monthly prayer letter with photos and updates, email Bowayj@aol.com.

      Paris, France · Cru

      Agape France

      Joe and Suzy Schlie direct Agape France, a French Protestant ministry with Cru that shares the Gospel with university students and young professionals. Joe is the son of former Bethlehem pastor Dave Schlie and his wife Elaine. Joe and Suzy have three daughters: Collette, Isabelle and Sophia.

      625,000+students in Paris, about 100,000 from other countries

      The ministry reaches students through music, the arts and sports, serves the city's homeless and refugees, and sends sports teams to share their faith in countries where evangelism is restricted.
